props.label: About Us
props.heading: An eye test, not a sales pitch
props.body:
We started as a single counter on FC Road fitting reading glasses, and the thing that kept people coming back was never the frames — it was that the test was unhurried and nobody was pushed into a lens they did not need.

Every eye test is done by a qualified optometrist on computerised equipment, and takes about twenty minutes. You get your prescription in writing whether or not you buy from us.

Our edging lab is in the store, so single-vision lenses are usually cut and fitted within the hour. Progressives and specialist coatings take two to three days because they are ordered to your exact measurements.

If a frame does not suit you, we will say so. That is the whole job.

props.label: The Collection
props.heading: Frames you will actually wear
props.sub: Pick your frame, then your lens — single vision, blue-cut or progressive. Prices include the frame and standard lenses; add your prescription at checkout or bring it in store.

items.title: Classic Metal Rectangle
items.desc: A slim stainless-steel rectangle with adjustable nose pads. The safest frame in the store — suits almost every face shape.
items.body:
If you are not sure what suits you, start here. A slim rectangular stainless-steel frame is the most forgiving shape there is — it flatters round, oval and square faces alike, and reads as smart rather than fashionable, which matters if these are your everyday work glasses.

The nose pads are adjustable, so the fit can be corrected in seconds if the frame slides. Spring hinges take the strain when you push them onto your head.

The price shown includes standard single-vision lenses. Choose blue-cut if you are on a screen all day, or progressive if you need both distance and reading in one lens.

Usually cut and fitted within the hour in single vision. Progressives take two to three working days.

items.title: Bold Acetate Square
items.desc: A thick hand-polished acetate square with a keyhole bridge. Makes a statement without shouting.
items.body:
Thick acetate in a squared-off shape, hand polished so the edges catch the light rather than looking flat. This is the frame people notice — good if you want your glasses to be part of how you dress rather than something you apologise for.

The keyhole bridge sits on the bridge of the nose rather than on pads, which suits a flatter nose profile and stops the frame sliding.

It is a wide fit at 145 mm, so it works better on broader faces. If you have a narrow face, the Classic Metal Rectangle or the Round Retro will sit better.

Includes standard single-vision lenses. Comes with a hard case and cloth.

items.title: Round Retro
items.desc: A slim round metal frame with a double bridge. Light on the face and easy to wear all day.
items.body:
A slim round metal frame with a double bridge — the shape that softens angular faces and has stayed in fashion for about a century, which is a reasonable sign it will still look right in three years.

At around 18 grams it is one of the lightest frames we stock, so it suits anyone who takes their glasses off because they get uncomfortable by the afternoon.

Round frames need a smaller lens area, which makes them a poor choice for a strong progressive — the corridor gets cramped. If your prescription is high, ask us before choosing this one.

Includes standard single-vision lenses, hard case and cloth.

productInfo.label: Note
productInfo.value: Ask us first for strong progressives

items.title: Cat-Eye Acetate
items.desc: An upswept cat-eye in layered acetate — lifts the face and works as well with a saree as with a shirt.
items.body:
An upswept cat-eye cut from layered acetate, so the colour changes slightly along the edge of the frame rather than sitting flat.

The lift at the outer corner draws the eye upward, which is why this shape is the usual recommendation for a rounder or heart-shaped face. It dresses up easily — it works with a saree at a wedding and with a shirt at the office, which most statement frames do not manage.

Medium width at 140 mm with a standard bridge. Comes with a hard case and cloth, and standard single-vision lenses included.

Available in blue-cut if you are at a screen all day, and in progressive.

items.title: Gold Slim Rimless
items.desc: A rimless frame on a slim gold temple — as close to wearing nothing as glasses get.
items.body:
Rimless titanium: the lens is mounted directly to the bridge and temples, so there is no frame outline on your face at all. If you want glasses that disappear in photographs, this is the one.

Titanium is both lighter and stronger than steel and does not corrode, which matters for a frame with this little material holding it together.

One honest caveat: rimless is the most fragile construction we sell, because all the stress goes through the mounting holes in the lens. It is not the right frame for a building site, a sport, or a small child in the house. Under normal office use it lasts years.

Not available in progressive — the lens shape does not leave enough depth. Bring your prescription and we will advise.

items.title: Colour Pop Collection
items.desc: Bright acetate frames for people who own more than one pair. Buy two and the second is half price.
items.body:
Glasses are the only medical device you wear on your face every day, so there is a reasonable argument for owning more than one pair. This range exists for that.

Bright acetate in four colours at a price that makes a second pair sensible rather than indulgent — one for work, one for the weekend, or a spare in the car so a lost pair is not a crisis.

Same construction as the rest of the range: spring hinges, standard single-vision lenses included, one-year warranty. The only thing that is cheaper is the frame material, not the lenses or the fitting.

Buy two frames from this collection and the second is half price. Ask in store or mention it when you order.

items.title: Polarised Sunglasses
items.desc: UV400 polarised sunglasses that cut glare off roads and water. Available with your prescription.
items.body:
Polarised lenses cut the horizontal glare that bounces off wet roads, car bonnets and water. The difference while driving in afternoon sun is the kind you notice immediately and cannot un-notice.

All lenses here are UV400, which blocks the full UVA and UVB range — worth knowing, because a dark lens without UV protection is worse than no sunglasses at all. It opens your pupil while letting the UV through.

Available plain or with your prescription ground in, so you are not choosing between seeing clearly and not squinting.

Prescription sunglasses take two to three working days. Plain tinted are available off the shelf the same day.

items.title: Monthly Contact Lenses
items.desc: Soft monthly disposables in a six-month box, fitted and taught in store before you take them home.
items.body:
Soft monthly disposables supplied in a six-month box, with the fitting consultation included in the price.

Contact lenses are not a shelf product. Your cornea has a curvature as individual as your prescription, and a lens that does not match it will feel fine for an hour and hurt by evening. We measure it, trial a lens, and only supply the box once it sits properly.

If you have not worn lenses before, we will teach you to insert, remove and store them in store, and you leave with a written care routine. That session takes about twenty minutes and is included.

Toric lenses are available if you have astigmatism — the price differs, so ask us. First-time wearers must have a fitting; we cannot ship a box without one.

items.q: Is the eye test really free?
items.a: Yes, the standard eye test is free with no obligation to buy, and you get the prescription in writing to take anywhere. Only the eye health screening, which includes a slit-lamp and retinal check, is charged separately at ₹300.

items.q: How long will my glasses take?
items.a: Standard single-vision lenses are cut in our own lab and are usually ready in about an hour. Progressives, high powers and specialist coatings are ordered to your measurements and take two to three working days.

items.q: Can I use a prescription from another optician or a hospital?
items.a: Yes, as long as it is less than a year old and includes your pupillary distance. If the PD is missing we will measure it here at no charge. Bring the prescription with you or send a photo on WhatsApp.

One year on manufacturing defects in the frame and on lens coatings peeling or crazing. It does not cover accidental damage, scratches from cleaning with a shirt, or a lost pair. Adjustments, nose pads and screws are free for life on anything bought here.

items.q: Can I return them if I don't get on with them?
items.a: Frames can be exchanged within 15 days in unused condition. Lenses ground to your prescription cannot be resold, so they are non-returnable, but if you are struggling to adapt to a new progressive, come back — that is usually a fitting adjustment, not a wrong lens.

items.q: Do you do home eye tests?
items.a: For elderly and mobility-restricted customers we test at home by appointment within the city, at no extra charge on a purchase. Call or WhatsApp to arrange one.

items.q: How often should I get my eyes tested?
items.a: Every two years for most adults, annually if you are over 40, diabetic, or your prescription has been changing. Children should be tested every year while their eyes are still developing.

notes:
CONTENT MODEL: Built as a modern eyewear retailer (Lensora Opticals) on FC Road, Pune, deliberately in the Lenskart mould — the frame catalogue is the centre of the site, with eye care as the trust layer that justifies buying there rather than online. FOUR pages via the recipe-level 'pages' array (consumed by api/sites/create.php): Home (/), Eyewear (/eyewear), Eye Care (/eye-care) and Contact (/contact). Header and footer link to those slugs, and per-page 'content' overrides retitle the shared products/services sections so they read differently on each page.

VIDEO: The home hero plays a muted, looping, autoplay background video of prescription glasses resting on a Landolt-C eye chart (videoUrl — a direct MP4 from Pexels) under a 0.58 overlay, rendering light-on-dark. No faces and no third-party branding in frame, which is why this clip was chosen over the eye-examination footage. The 'image' field is the static fallback. Swap both for the store's own footage before going live.

PRODUCTS: Eight items exercise the full products manifest — nested attributes, per-combination variants with SKU, MRP and live stock, body copy, productInfo tables and slugs for individual product pages. The attribute axes are the ones this trade actually sells on: Frame Colour x Lens Type (single vision / blue-cut / progressive) for eyeglasses, Lens Tint x Plain-vs-Prescription for sunglasses, Wear x Power for contact lenses. Rimless is deliberately offered WITHOUT a progressive option because the lens depth genuinely does not allow it — the copy says so rather than silently omitting it. The last variant of each product is stock 0 to exercise the out-of-stock and disabled add-to-cart states.

PRICING: Set at realistic Indian optical retail levels for mid-2026 — frames with standard lenses from Rs 999, blue-cut around Rs 700 more, progressives Rs 4,499-5,099, polarised sunglasses Rs 1,499 plain and Rs 3,299 with prescription, monthly contact lenses Rs 1,199 for a six-month box. Verify against the store's own rate card before going live.

COPY ANGLE: The decisive objection in optical retail is 'am I being upsold?', so the site leans hard the other way — free test with the prescription given in writing whether or not you buy, an explicit 'no commission on upgrades' pillar, a review about being talked OUT of a coating, an FAQ answering whether blue-cut actually works, and an honest warning that rimless is the most fragile construction sold. Keep that posture if the copy is rewritten; it is what differentiates a local optician from an online seller.

IMAGES: All photos are hosted Pexels CDN URLs (https://images.pexels.com/photos/<id>/pexels-photo-<id>.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=...). SiteRenderer::media passes any http(s) URL through untouched. EVERY URL here was downloaded and visually inspected before use — the deterministic Pexels filename pattern 404s for some ids, so never add one without fetching it first. All should be replaced with the store's own product photography before going live, especially the frame shots, which must match actual stock.

NO TEAM SECTION: Omitted deliberately, following the salon/gym/wedding convention of not pairing stock photographs with invented staff names.
